Six Propositions Concerning Satan

And now, to forestall objections, I will lay down some propositions, or conclusions, concerning Satan and his devices, and then give you the reasons of the point, and so come to make some use and application of the whole to ourselves.

The first proposition or conclusion I will lay down is this.

That though Satan has his devices to draw souls to sin, yet we must be careful that we do not lay all our temptations on Satan, that we do not wrong the devil and father on him what is to be fathered on our own base hearts. I think that men often charge on the devil what is to be charged on their own hearts. “Then the Lord God said to the617 woman, ‘What is this you have done?’ ‘The serpent deceived me,’ she replied, ‘and I ate.’” Sin and shifting the blame came into the world together. It is no small baseness of our hearts that they will be wicked, yes, very wicked, and yet will father that wickedness on Satan. Man has an evil root within him, so that, were there no devil to tempt him, nor any wicked men in the world to entice him, yet that root of bitterness, that cursed sinful nature that is in him, would draw him to sin, though he knows beforehand that the wages of sin is eternal death. “For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery,618 sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.” The whole frame of man is619 out of frame. The understanding is dark, the will perverse, the memory slippery, the affections crooked, the conscience corrupted, the tongue poisoned, and the heart wholly evil, only evil, and continually evil. Should God chain up Satan, and give him no liberty to tempt or entice the sons of men to vanity and folly, yet they would not refrain, indeed they could not help sinning against him, by reason of that cursed nature that is in them, which will always be provoking620 them to those sins that will provoke and stir up the anger and wrath of God against them. Satan has only a persuading sleight, not an enforcing might. He may tempt us, but without ourselves he cannot conquer us; he621 may entice us, but without ourselves he cannot hurt us. Our hearts have the greatest part in every sin. Satan622 can never ruin a man without the man himself, but a man may easily ruin himself without Satan. Satan can only present the golden cup; he has no power to force us to drink the poison that is in the cup. He can only present to us the glory of the world; he cannot force us to fall down and worship him in order to enjoy the world. He can only spread his snares; he has no power to force us to walk in the midst of his snares. Therefore do the devil so much justice as not to excuse yourselves+ by accusing him, and laying on him the load that you+ should lay on your+ own hearts.

The second proposition is this.

That Satan has a great hand and part in most sins. It was Satan who623 tempted our first parents to rebellion. It was Satan who provoked David to624 number the people. It was Satan who put Peter up to rebuking Christ; that is why Christ says, “Get behind Me, Satan!”625 It was Satan who put Cain up to murdering righteous Abel; that is why he is called “a murderer from626 the beginning.” It was Satan who put treason against Christ into the heart of Judas: “The evening meal was underway, and the devil627 had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus.” It was Satan who put Ananias up to lying. Peter said,628 “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit?” As the hand of Joab was in the story of the woman of Tekoa, so Satan’s hand is usually in all the sins that men commit. Such is Satan’s malice against God, and his envy629 against man, that he will have a hand one way or another in all their sins, though he knows that all the sins that he provokes others to will be charged on him, to his greater woe and eternal torment. Ambrose brings in the devil boasting against Christ and claiming Judas as his own: “He is not yours, Lord Jesus; he is mine. His thoughts are set on me. He eats with you, but is fed by me. He takes bread from you, but money from me. He drinks wine with you, and sells your blood to me.” Such is his malice against Christ, and his wrath and rage against man, that he will take every advantage to draw men to what may give him the advantage to triumph over Christ and men’s souls forever.

The third proposition is this.

That Satan must have a double leave before he can do anything against us. He must have leave from God, and leave from ourselves, before he can act anything against our happiness. He must have his commission from God, as you may see in the example of Job. Though630 the devil had malice enough to destroy him, yet he did not have so much as the power to touch him till God gave him a commission.

The devils could not so much as enter631 the swine without leave from Christ. Satan would gladly have fought with Peter, but he could not do this without leave: “Satan has asked to sift you+.”632 So Satan could never have overthrown Ahab and Saul but by633 a commission from God. Ah, what a heart-medicine, what a comfort this should be to the saints, that their greatest, most cunning, and most watchful enemy cannot hurt or harm them without leave from him who is their sweetest Savior, their dearest husband, and their choicest friend!

And as Satan must have leave from634 God, so he must have leave from us. When he tempts, we must assent; when he makes offers, we must listen; when he commands, we must obey; or else all his labor and temptations will be in vain, and the evil that he tempts us to will be put down to his account alone. There is a remarkable passage of the apostle in Acts 5:3: “Why has Satan635 filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit?” etc.

He does not remonstrate with Satan. He does not say, “Satan, why636 have you filled Ananias’ heart to make him lie to the Holy Spirit?” But he remonstrates with Ananias. Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit?” Why have you given him an advantage to fill your heart with unbelief, hypocrisy, and obstinate audacity, to lie to the Holy Spirit? As if he had said, “Satan could never have done this in you (which will now ruin you forever) unless you had first given him leave.” If, when a temptation comes, a man cries out and says, “Ah, Lord! Here is a temptation that would force me, that would deflower my soul, and I have no strength to withstand it. Oh, help, help, for your honor’s sake, for your Son’s sake, for your promise’s sake!” it is a sign that Satan has not gained your+ consent, but has committed a rape on your+ souls, which he will pay for dearly.

The fourth proposition is this.

That no weapons but spiritual weapons will be useful and serviceable to the soul in fighting and combating with the devil. The apostle shows this: “Therefore take up” (says637 he) “the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you+ will be able to stand your+ ground, and having done everything, to stand.” So the same apostle tells you+ that “the weapons of your+ warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to638 demolish strongholds.” You+ have to deal not with a weak but with a mighty639 enemy. And therefore you+ need to see to it that your+ weapons are mighty, and that they cannot be unless they are spiritual. Carnal weapons have no might or spirit in them toward making a conquest of Satan. It was not David’s sling or stone that gave him the honor and advantage of setting his feet on Goliath, but his faith in the name of the Lord of Hosts: “You come640 against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the Lord of Hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.” He who641 fights against Satan in the strength of his own resolutions, constitution, or upbringing will certainly flee and fall before him. Satan will be too hard for such a soul, and lead him captive at his pleasure. The only way to stand, conquer, and triumph is always to plead, “It is written,” as Christ did. There is no sword but the two-edged sword of the642 Spirit that will be found to be proven metal when a soul comes to engage Satan. Therefore, when you+ are tempted to uncleanness, plead, “It is written, ‘Be holy, because I am holy.’ And643 ‘let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.’” If he tempts you+ to distrust God’s providence and fatherly care of you+, plead, “It is written, ‘Those644 who fear the Lord lack no good thing.’ It is written, ‘The Lord gives645 grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.’” If he tempts you+ to fear that you+ will faint and fall, and never be able to run to the end of the race that is set before646 you+, plead, “It is written, ‘The righteous one holds to his way, and the one with clean hands grows stronger.’ It is written, ‘I will make an everlasting covenant with them: I will never turn away647 from doing good to them, and I will put My fear in their hearts, so that they will never turn away from Me.’ It is written, ‘Those who wait upon the Lord will renew their648 strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.’” If Satan tempts you+ to think that, because your+ sun is for the present set in a cloud, it will therefore rise no more, that the face of God will shine on you+ no more, that your+ best days are now at an end, and that you+ must spend all your+ time in sorrow and sighing, plead, “It is written, ‘He will turn again;649 He will have compassion on us, and cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.’ It is written, ‘For a brief moment I forsook650 you, but with great compassion I will bring you back.651 In a little anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you,’ says the Lord your Redeemer. It is written, ‘Though the mountains may be652 removed and the hills may be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not be broken,’ says the Lord, who has compassion on you. It is written, ‘Can a woman653 forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you! Behold, I have inscribed you on the654 palms of My hands; your walls are ever before Me.’” If ever you+ would be too hard for Satan, and have your+ bow still remain in strength after all the assaults on you+, then take up the word of God, “which is the two-edged sword of the Spirit,”655 and “the shield of faith, with which you+ will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the devil.” It is not spitting at Satan’s name, nor crossing yourselves+, nor leaning on your+ own resolutions, that will get you+ the victory.

Luther reports of Staupitz, a German minister, that he acknowledged that before he came to understand rightly the free and powerful grace of God, he vowed and resolved a hundred times against some particular sin, and could never get power over it. At last he saw the reason to be his trusting in his own resolution. Therefore be skillful in the word of righteousness, and in the acting of faith on Christ and his victory, and on that crown of glory that is set before you+, and Satan will certainly “flee from you+,”656 etc.

The fifth proposition is this.

That we may read much of Satan’s nature and disposition in the various names and titles that are given him in the Scriptures. Sometimes he is called Behemoth, that is, bruta [brute beasts], by which657 the greatness and brutishness of the devil is pictured. Those evil spirits are sometimes called διάβολοι, accusers, for their slanders and false charges; and πονηροί, evil ones, for their malice. Satan is Adversarius, an adversary who troubles658 and harasses; Abaddon is a destroyer. They are called tempters for their suggestions, lions for their devouring, dragons for their cruelty, and serpents for their cunning, etc. As his names are, so is he. As face answers to face, so Satan’s names answer to his nature. He has the worst names and the worst nature of all created creatures, etc.

The sixth and last proposition is this.

That God will soon tread659 Satan down under the saints’ feet. Christ our champion has already won the field, and will soon set our feet on the necks of our spiritual enemies. Satan is a defeated adversary; Christ has led him captive and triumphed over him on the cross. Christ has already overcome him, and has put weapons into your+ hands, so that you+ may overcome him too and set your+ feet on his neck. Though Satan is a roaring lion, yet Christ, who is “the Lion of the tribe of Judah,” will make Satan flee and fall before you+. Let Satan do his worst, yet you+ will have the honor and the happiness of triumphing over him. Cheer up, you+ precious sons of Zion, for the certainty and sweetness of victory will abundantly repay you+ for all the pains you+ have taken in resisting Satan’s temptations. The broken horns of Satan will be trumpets of our triumph and the cornets of our joy, etc.

The Reasons of the Point

Now I will come to the reasons of the point, and so draw to a close, etc.

The first reason is, that the saints’ hearts may be kept in a humble, praying,660 watching frame. Oh, has Satan so many devices to ensnare and ruin the souls of men? How this should awaken dull, drowsy souls, and make them stand on their watch! A saint should be like a seraph, covered all over with eyes and lights, so that he may avoid Satan’s snares and stand firm in the hour of temptation. The Lord has revealed in the Scripture the various snares, plots, and devices that the devil has to ruin the souls of men, so that, being forewarned, they may be forearmed, and may always be on their watchtower, holding their weapons in their hands, as the Jews did in Nehemiah’s time, etc.

The second reason is, from the malice, envy, and enmity that is in Satan661 against the souls of men. Satan is full of envy and enmity, and that makes him very diligent to suit his snares and plots to the temperaments, constitutions, fancies, and callings of men, so that he may make them as miserable as himself. The Russians are so malicious that a man will hide some of his own goods in the house of the man he hates, and then accuse him of stealing them. So Satan, out of malice to662 the souls of men, hides his goods, his wares, as I may say, in the souls of men, and then goes and accuses them before the Lord. And Satan’s malice, envy, and enmity drive him to a thousand thousand other ways to ruin the precious souls of men eternally, etc.

The third reason is drawn from the long experience that Satan has had. He is a spirit of mighty abilities, and his abilities to lay snares before us are mightily increased by his long standing. He is a spirit of more than five thousand years’ standing. He has had time enough to study all the ways and methods that most tend to ensnare and ruin the souls of men. And as he has had time enough, so he has made it his whole aim, his only aim, his constant aim, to find out snares, depths, and stratagems to entangle and overthrow the souls of men. When he was only a young serpent, he easily deceived and outwitted our first parents; but now he has grown into that old serpent, as663 John speaks. He is as old as the world,664 and has grown very cunning by experience.

The fourth reason is, in judgment on the men of the world, that they may stumble, and fall, and be ensnared forever. Wicked men who withstand the offers of mercy and despise the Spirit of grace, who will not open, however hard God knocks by his word and rod, by his Spirit and conscience, are given up by a hand of justice to be665 hardened, deceived, and ensnared by Satan to their everlasting ruin. And what can be more just than that they should be taken and charmed by Satan’s wiles, who have often refused to be charmed by the Spirit of grace, though he has charmed ever so wisely and ever so sweetly, etc.?

The fifth reason is, that the excellence and power of God’s grace may be the more displayed and made known, by making man able to grapple with this mighty adversary; and that, notwithstanding all the plots, devices, and stratagems of Satan, God will make his people victorious here and crown them with glory hereafter. The greater and more cunning the enemies of the children of Israel were, the more God’s power, wisdom, and goodness sparkled and shone, in that, notwithstanding all their power, plots, and stratagems, etc., he would bring them to Canaan at last. When Paul had well weighed this, he sits down and glories in his infirmities,666 and distresses, and Satan’s buffetings, so that the power of Christ might rest on him.

The Use: Ten Helps Against All His Devices

The use of the point.

IF Satan has such a world of devices and stratagems to ensnare and ruin the souls of men, then instead of wondering that so few are saved, sit down and wonder that any are saved, that any escape the snares of this cunning fowler, who spreads his nets and casts out his baits in all places, and in all cases and companies, etc.

But this is not the main thing that I intend to speak to. My main business will be to set before you+ some special rules and helps against all his devices, and the first is this.

If you+ do not want to be taken by any of Satan’s devices, then walk by rule. He who walks by rule walks most safely;667 he who walks by rule walks most honorably; he who walks by rule walks most sweetly. When men throw off the word, then God throws them off, and then Satan takes them by the hand and leads them into snares at his pleasure. He who thinks himself too good to be ruled by the word will be found too bad to be acknowledged by God; and if God does not and will not acknowledge him, Satan will overthrow him by his stratagems. Those who keep to the rule will be kept in the hour of temptation: “Because668 you have kept My word of patient endurance, I will also keep you from the hour of temptation that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.”

2. As you+ would not be taken with any of Satan’s devices, beware of vexing669 and grieving the Holy Spirit of God. It is the Spirit of the Lord Jesus Christ who is best able to reveal Satan’s snares to us. It is he alone who can point out all Satan’s plots, and reveal all his methods, and enable men to escape the pits that Satan has dug for their precious souls. Ah souls! If you+ set that sweet and blessed Spirit mourning, who alone can secure you+ from Satan’s depths, by whom will you+ be secured? Man is a weak creature, and in no way able to detect Satan’s snares or to avoid them, unless the Spirit of the Lord gives him skill and power. Therefore, whoever else is grieved, make sure the Spirit is not grieved by your+ gross sins, nor by your+ refusing670 the heart-reviving medicines and comforts that he sets before you+, nor by slighting and despising his gracious workings in others,671 nor by calling sincerity hypocrisy, and faith fancy, etc., nor by fathering on the Spirit the things that are the offspring and fruits of your+ own hearts. The Spirit of the Lord is your+ counselor, your+ comforter, your+ upholder, your+ strengthener. It is only the Spirit who makes a man too great for Satan to conquer. “Greater is He who is in you+672 than he who is in the world.”

Thirdly, if you+ do not want to be taken with any of Satan’s devices, then labor for more heavenly wisdom. Ah souls!673 You+ are much in the dark. You+ have only a little compared with what others have, and with what you+ might have had, had you+ not failed yourselves+. There are many knowing souls, but only a few wise souls. There is often a great deal of knowledge where there is only a little wisdom to make use of that knowledge. Knowledge without wisdom674 is like mettle in a blind horse, which is often the cause of the rider’s fall and of his bones being knocked against the walls. It is not the most knowing Christian, but the wisest Christian, who sees, avoids and escapes Satan’s snares. “The path of life leads upward675 for the wise,” says Solomon, “that he may avoid going down to Sheol.” Heavenly wisdom makes a man delight to fly high; and the higher any man flies, the more he is out of the reach of Satan’s snares. Ah souls! You+ need a great deal676 of heavenly wisdom to see where and how Satan lays his baits and snares, and wisdom to find out proper remedies against his devices, and wisdom to apply those remedies seasonably, inwardly and effectually to your+ own hearts, so that you+ may avoid the snares which that evil one has laid for your+ precious souls.

4. If you+ do not want to be taken with any of Satan’s devices, then resist Satan’s first stirrings at once. It is safe to resist; it is dangerous to dispute. Eve disputes, and falls in Paradise;677 Job resists, and conquers on the dunghill. He who will play with Satan’s bait will quickly be taken with Satan’s hook. The promise of conquest is made to resisting, not to disputing: “Resist the devil, and he will flee678 from you+.” Ah souls! If you+ were better at resisting than at disputing (though perhaps you+ are not very expert at either), your+ temptations would be fewer, and your+ strength to stand would be greater than it now is, etc.

Fifthly, if you+ do not want to be taken with any of Satan’s devices, then labor to be filled with the Spirit. The Spirit of the Lord is a Spirit of light and power, and what can a soul do without light, and power against “the spiritual forces of evil679 in the heavenly realms”? It is not enough that you+ have the Spirit; you+ must be filled with the Spirit, or else that evil spirit, Satan, will be too hard for you+, and his plots will prosper against you+. That is a sweet word of the apostle,680 “be filled with the Spirit”; that is, labor for an abundance of the Spirit. He who thinks he has enough of the Holy Spirit will quickly find himself overcome by the evil spirit. Satan has his snares to take you+ in prosperity and adversity, in health and sickness, in strength and weakness; when you+ are alone and when you+ are in company; when you+ come to spiritual duties and when you+ come away from spiritual duties. And if you+ are not filled with the Spirit, Satan will be too hard and too crafty for you+, and will easily and frequently take you+ in his snares and make a prey of you+ in spite of yourselves+. Therefore labor more to have your+ hearts filled with the Spirit than to have your+ heads filled with notions, your+ shops with goods, your+ chests with silver, or your+ bags with gold. So you+ will escape the snares of this fowler and triumph over all his plots, etc.

Sixthly, if you+ do not want to be taken in any of Satan’s snares, then keep humble.681 A humble heart will rather lie in the dust than rise by wickedness, and will sooner part with everything than with the peace of a good conscience. Humility keeps the soul free from many of the darts Satan casts and the snares he spreads, as the low shrubs are free from many violent gusts and blasts of wind that shake and tear the taller trees. The devil has least power to fasten a temptation on the man who is most humble. He who has a gracious measure of humility is neither moved by Satan’s offers nor terrified by his threats. I have read of one who, seeing in a vision many snares of the devil spread on the earth, sat down and mourned, and said to himself (Quis pertransiet ista), “Who will pass through these?” To this he heard a voice answer (humilitas pertransiet), “Humility will.” God has said that he will teach the humble,682 and that he will dwell with the humble, and that he will fill and satisfy the humble. And if the teachings of God, the indwellings of God, the pourings-in of God will not keep the soul from falling into Satan’s snares, I do not know what will. And therefore, as you+ would be happy in resisting Satan, and blessed in triumphing over Satan and all his snares, keep humble; I say again, keep humble, etc.

7. If you+ do not want to be taken in any of Satan’s snares, then keep a strong, close and constant watch. A careless683 soul is already an ensnared soul. The soul that will not watch against temptations will certainly fall before the power of temptations. Satan works most strongly on the imagination when the soul is drowsy. The soul’s carelessness is Satan’s opportunity to fall on the soul and to plunder the soul, as Joshua did the men of Ai. The best way to be safe and secure from all Satan’s assaults is, with Nehemiah and the Jews, to watch and pray, and pray and watch. By this means they became too hard for their enemies, and the work of the Lord prospered sweetly in their hands. Remember how Christ rebuked his sluggish disciples: “What, were you+ not able to keep watch with684 Me for one hour?” “What, can you+ not watch with me? How then will you+ die with me?” If you+ cannot endure words, how will you+ endure wounds, etc.? Satan always keeps a crafty and malicious watch, “seeking someone to devour” (katapie), or685 whom he may drink or sip up, as the686 apostle speaks in 1 Pet 5:8. Satan687 is very envious of our condition, that we should enjoy that Paradise out of which he is cast, and out of which he will be kept forever.

Shall Satan keep a crafty watch, and688 shall Christians not keep a holy, spiritual watch? Our whole life is beset with temptations. Satan watches every opportunity to break our peace, to wound our consciences, to lessen our comforts, to weaken our graces, to blur our evidences and to dampen our assurances, etc. Oh, what need then we have to be always on our watchtower, lest we be overtaken by this subtle serpent! Watchfulness includes a waking, a rousing up of the soul. It is a continual, careful observing of our hearts and ways, in all the turnings of our lives, so that we always keep close to God and his word.

Watchfulness is nothing else but the soul running up and down, to and fro, busy everywhere. It is the heart busied and employed in diligent observation of (Quid inde) what comes from within us, and of (Quid unde) what comes from outside us and into us. Ah souls! You+ are safe and secure only as long as you+ are on your+ watch. While Antipater kept the watch, Alexander was safe; and while we keep a strict watch, we are safe. A watchful soul is a soul on the wing, a soul out of gunshot, a soul on a rock, a soul in a castle, a soul above the clouds, a soul held fast in everlasting arms.

I will conclude this seventh head with this advice. Remember, the dragon is subtle: it bites the elephant’s ear and then sucks his blood, because it knows that to be the only place which the elephant cannot reach with his trunk to defend. So our enemies are so subtle that they will bite us and strike us where they can do us the most harm; and therefore it greatly concerns us to stand always on our guard.

Eighthly, if you+ do not want to be taken with any of Satan’s snares and devices, then keep up your+ communion with God. Your+ strength to stand against and withstand689 Satan’s fiery darts comes from your+ communion with God. A soul high in communion with God may be tempted, but will not easily be conquered; such a soul will fight it out to the death. Communion with God furnishes the soul with the greatest and choicest arguments to withstand Satan’s temptations. Communion is the result of union. Communion is a mutual exchange between Christ and a gracious soul. Communion is Jacob’s ladder, where you+ have Christ sweetly coming down into the soul, and the soul, by divine influences, sweetly ascending up to Christ. Communion with Christ is very inflaming, raising and strengthening. While Samson kept up his communion690 with God, no enemy could stand before him, but he goes on conquering and to conquer; but when he had fallen in his communion with God, he quickly falls before the plots of his enemies. It will be so with your+ souls: so long as your+ communion with God is kept up, you+ will be too hard for “the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms”; but if you+ fall from your+691 communion with God, you+ will fall like others before the face of every temptation. David, so long as he kept up his communion with God, stands and triumphs over all his enemies; but when he had fallen in his communion with God, then he falls before the enemies that were in his own bosom, and flees before those who pursued his life. It will be so with your+ souls if you+ do not keep up your+ communion with God. Job keeps up his communion with God, and conquers Satan on the dunghill. Adam loses his communion with God, and is conquered by Satan in Paradise. Communion with God is a shield on land as well as an anchor at sea; it is a sword to defend you+ as well as a staff to support you+. Therefore keep up your+ communion.

9. If you+ do not want to be taken in any of Satan’s snares, then do not engage Satan in your+ own strength, but692 be every day drawing new power and strength from the Lord Jesus. Certainly the soul that engages any old or new temptation without new strength, new influences from on high, will fall before the power of the temptation. You+ may see this in Peter. He rested on some old strength he had received (“Though all men should deny you, yet I will not”), and therefore he falls sadly before a new temptation: he curses and693 swears, and denies him three times who had three times appeared gloriously to him. Ah souls! When the snare is spread, look up to Jesus Christ, who is lifted up in the gospel as the bronze serpent was694 in the wilderness, and say to him, “Dear Lord, here is a new snare laid to catch my soul, and the grace I received before, without fresh supplies from your blessed bosom, will not deliver me from this snare. Oh, give me new strength, new power, new influences, new measures of grace, so that I may escape this snare.” Ah souls! Remember this: your+695 strength to stand and overcome must not be expected from graces received, but from the fresh and renewed influences of heaven. You+ must lean more on Christ than on your+ duties; you+ must lean more on Christ than on spiritual tastes and manifestations; you+ must lean more on Christ than on your+ graces, or else Satan will lead you+ into captivity, etc.

Tenthly and lastly, if you+ do not want to be taken in any of Satan’s snares, then be much in prayer. Prayer is a shelter to the soul, a sacrifice to God and a scourge to the devil. David’s heart was often more out of tune than his harp: he prays, and then, in spite696 of the devil, cries, “Return to your rest, O my soul.” Prayer is (Porta coeli, clavis Paradisi) the gate of heaven, a key to let us into Paradise. There is nothing that makes plots fruitless like prayer; therefore Christ says, “Watch and pray so that you+ will not enter into temptation.” You+ must watch and pray, and pray and watch, if you+ do not want to enter into temptation. When Sennacherib and Haman had laid plots and snares to destroy the Jews, they prayed, and their souls were delivered, and Sennacherib and Haman were destroyed. David had many snares laid for him, and this drives him to prayer: “Keep me,” he says, “from the snares they have laid for me,697 and from the lures of evildoers. Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I escape.” “The proud,” he says, “hide a snare for me; the cords of their net are spread along the path, and lures are set698 out for me. Selah. I say to the Lord, ‘You are my God.’ Hear, O Lord, my cry for help.”699 Saul and many others had laid snares for David, and this drives him to prayer; and so the snares are broken, and he is delivered. Ah souls! Take words with you+, and tell God that Satan has spread his snares in all places and in all companies; tell God that he digs deep, and that he has plot upon plot and device upon device, and all to700 ruin you+; tell God that you+ have neither skill nor power to escape his snares; tell God that it is a work too high and too hard for any created being to work your+ deliverance, unless he puts his own everlasting arms under you+; tell God how his honor is pledged to stand by you+ and to bring you+ off safe, so that you+ are not ruined by Satan’s plots; tell God how the wicked would triumph if you+ should fall into Satan’s snares; tell God of the love of Christ, of the blood of Christ, and of the intercession of Christ for you+, so that a way may be found for your+ escape; tell God that if he will make it his honor to save you+ from falling into Satan’s snares, you+ will make it your+ glory to speak of his goodness and to live out his kindness. Christians must do as Daedalus did, who, when he could not escape by a way on earth, went by a way of heaven; and that is the way of prayer, which is the only way left to escape Satan’s snares, etc.

The next use is a use of thankfulness, for those who escape Satan’s snares, who are not taken by him at his will. Ah Christians! It is your+ duty, with that princely prophet David, to call on your+ souls and say, “Bless the701 Lord, O our souls; all that is within us, bless His holy name. Bless the Lord, O our souls, and do not forget all His kind deeds,” who has not given us up to be a prey to Satan, and to be ensnared by the snares that he has laid for our souls. The sense of this great favor worked up David’s heart to praises: “Blessed be the Lord,” he says,702 “who has not given us as prey to their teeth. We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler; the snare is broken, and we have escaped.” Ah Christians! Remember that the greatest part of the world, indeed the greatest part of professing Christians, are taken in Satan’s snares. Can you+ think seriously of this and not703 blush to be unthankful? What are you+ better than others? And what have you+ deserved of God, or done for God, more than others, that you+ should by the help of a divine hand escape the snares, when others are taken and held in the snares of the devil, to their eternal704 overthrow, etc.?

Will you+ be thankful for escaping the snares that men spread for your+ lives or property, etc.? And will you+ not be much more thankful for escaping the snares that Satan has laid for your+ precious souls?

Remember this: deliverance705 from Satan’s snares carries with it the clearest and the greatest evidence that the soul and heart of God are toward you+. Many a man, by a common hand of providence, escapes many a snare that man has laid for him, and yet does not escape the snares that Satan has laid for him. Saul and Judas and Demas no doubt escaped many snares that men had laid for them, but none of them escaped the snares that the devil had laid for them. Many men are lifted above the snares of men by a common hand of providence who are left to fall into the snares of the devil by a hand of justice. Your+ deliverance from Satan’s snares is a fruit of special love. Can you+ look on it like this and not be thankful, O precious souls? I think not.

The last use of this point is to call on Christians to long to be at home. Oh, long to be in the bosom of Christ; long to be in the land of Canaan; for706 this world, this wilderness, is full of snares; all employments are full of snares, and all enjoyments are full of snares. In the things of this life Satan has his snares to entrap us, and in all spiritual things Satan has his snares to catch us. All places are full of snares: city and country, shop and private chamber, sea and land; and all our blessings are surrounded with snares. There are snares about our tables and snares about our beds, etc. Indeed, Satan is so powerful and subtle that he will often make our greatest, nearest and dearest blessings become our greatest snares. Sometimes he will make the wife who lies in a man’s bosom a snare to him, as Samson’s was, and as Job’s was; sometimes he will make the child a snare, as Absalom was, and Eli’s sons were; and sometimes he will make the servant a snare, as Joseph was to his master’s wife. Ah souls! Satan is so cunning and artful that he can turn your+ cups into snares, and your+ clothes into snares, and your+ houses into snares, and your+ gardens into snares, and all your+ recreations into snares, etc. And oh, how the consideration of these things should move all your+ souls to say with the church, “Make haste, my707 beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices,” and to love and look and long for the coming of Christ! Shall the betrothed maiden long for the wedding day, the servant for his freedom, the captive for his ransom, the traveler for his inn, the708 sailor for his harbor? And shall not the people of the Lord long much more to be in the bosom of Christ? There is nothing below the bosom of Christ that is not surrounded with Satan’s snares.

What Paul once said of chains and709 afflictions, that they attended him in every place, all the saints may say of Satan’s snares, that they attend them in every place. This should make them cry out (migremus hinc, migremus hinc), “Let us go from here, let us go from here,” and say with Monica, Augustine’s mother,710 “What are we doing here? Why do we not depart from here? Why do we not fly away more swiftly?” Ah souls! Until you+ are taken up into the bosom of Christ, your+ comforts will not be full, pure and constant. Until then Satan will always be tempting you+ and spreading snares to entangle you+; therefore you+ should always be crying out with the church, “Come, Lord711 Jesus!” Is not Christ that star of Jacob that gives light to those who are in darkness? That Prince of Peace, who brings the olive branch of peace to souls that are entangled? Is not the greatest worth and wealth in him? Are not all the lesser excellencies and perfections of all created beings summed up in him? Is he not the crown of crowns, the glory of glories and the heaven of heavens? Oh then, be always longing after a full, clear and constant enjoyment of Christ in heaven; for until then, Satan will always have plots and designs on you+. He acts by an untiring power, and will never let you+ rest until you+ are taken up to an everlasting rest in the bosom of Christ.

669. Spiritus Sanctus est res delicata, the divine Spirit is a very tender thing; if you+ grieve him, he will certainly grieve and vex your+ precious souls. Lam 1:16.

676. Malim prudentiae guttam quam foecundioris fortunae pelagus [I would rather have a drop of prudence than an ocean of richer fortune], said Nazianzen. A serpent’s eye is a rare ornament in a dove’s head.

681. It is reported of Satan that he said this of a learned man (tu me semper vincis): “You always overcome me. When I would exalt and promote you, you keep yourself in humility; and when I would throw you down, you lift yourself up in assurance of faith.”

684. Matt 24:42 ch. 26:41. Mark 13:33, 34, 35, 37. Luke 21:36.

692. That is a remarkable saying of Moses, Exod 15: God is fortitudo mea, and laus mea, and salus mea, my strength, and my praise, and my salvation, all in the abstract.

Appendix. Five More Devices to Keep Souls from Christ

1. The Greatness of Sin

An Appendix concerning five more separate devices that Satan has to keep poor souls from believing in Christ, from receiving Christ, from embracing Christ, from resting, leaning, or relying on Christ for everlasting happiness and blessedness, according to the gospel; and remedies against those devices.

Now the first device that Satan has to keep the soul back from believing in Christ, from embracing Christ, etc. is,

BY suggesting to the soul the greatness and vileness of his sins. “What,” says Satan, “do you think that you will ever obtain mercy through Christ, you who have sinned so high-handedly against Christ? You who have slighted the offers of grace? You who have grieved the Spirit of grace? You who have despised the word of grace? You who have trampled underfoot the blood of the covenant, by which you might have been pardoned, purged, justified, and saved? You who have spoken and done all the evil that you could? No, no,” says Satan, “he has mercy for others,712 but not for you; pardon for others, but not for you; righteousness for others, but not for you, etc. Therefore it is vain for you to think of believing in Christ, or of resting and leaning your guilty soul on Christ.”

Now the remedies against this device of Satan are as follows.

The first remedy against this device of Satan is to consider that the greater your+ sins are, the more you+ need a Savior; the greater your+ burden is, the more you+ need someone to help you+ bear it. The deeper the wound is, the more need there is of the surgeon; the more dangerous the disease is, the more need there is of the physician. Who but madmen will argue like this: “My burden is great, therefore I will not call out for help; my wound is713 deep, therefore I will not call out for balm; my disease is dangerous, therefore I will not go to the physician”? Ah! It is spiritual madness; it is the devil’s logic to argue like this: “My sins are great, therefore I will not go to Christ; I dare not rest or lean on Christ,” etc. But the soul should reason like this: “The greater my sins are, the more I need mercy, pardon; and therefore I will go to Christ, who delights714 in mercy, who pardons sin for his own name’s sake, who is as able and as715 willing to forgive pounds as pence, thousands as hundreds.”

The second remedy against this device of Satan is to consider solemnly that the promise of grace and mercy is to returning souls. And therefore, however wicked you are, yet if you will return, God will be yours, mercy will be yours, and pardon yours, etc. 2 Chr 30:9: “For if you+ return to the Lord,716 your+ brothers and sons will receive mercy in the presence of their captors and will return to this land. For the Lord your+ God is gracious and merciful; He will not turn His face away from you+ if you+ return to Him.” So Jer 3:12:717 “Go, proclaim this message toward the north: ‘Return, O faithless Israel,’ declares the Lord. ‘I will no longer look on you+ with anger, for I am merciful,’ declares the Lord. ‘I will not be angry forever.’” So Joel 2:13: “Rend your+718 hearts and not your+ garments, and return to the Lord your+ God. For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion. And He relents from sending disaster.” So Isa 55:7: “Let the wicked man forsake his own way and the unrighteous man his own thoughts; let him return to the Lord, and He will have mercy on him, and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon”; or, as the Hebrew reads it, he will multiply pardons. So Ezek719 18.

Ah sinner! It is not your great transgressions that will shut you out from mercy, if you will break off your sins by repentance and return to the fountain of mercy. Christ’s heart, Christ’s arms, are wide open to embrace the returning prodigal. It is not simply the greatest of your sins, but your obstinate persisting in sin, that will be your eternal overthrow.

The third remedy against this device of Satan is to consider seriously that the greatest sinners have obtained mercy; and therefore all the angels in heaven, all the men on earth, and all the devils in hell cannot say that you will not obtain mercy. Manasseh was a notorious sinner.720 He set up altars for Baal; he worshiped and served all the host of heaven. He made his sons pass through the fire; he gave himself to witchcraft and sorcery; he made Judah sin more wickedly than the heathen did, whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel; he721 made the streets of Jerusalem run down with innocent blood, etc. Ah! What a devil incarnate he was in his actions! And yet when he humbled himself and sought the Lord, the Lord listened to his plea, and heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem, and made himself known to him, and crowned him with mercy and loving-kindness, as you may see in 2 Chr722 33. So Paul was once “a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man,” yet he723 “obtained mercy.” So Mary Magdalene was a724 notorious prostitute, a common whore, one out of whom Christ cast seven devils; yet she is pardoned by Christ and dearly loved by Christ (Luke 7). So725 in Mark 16:9: “Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.” Jansenius, on the passage, says that it is very noteworthy that our Savior after his resurrection appeared first to Mary Magdalene and to Peter, who had been grievous sinners, so that even the worst of sinners may be comforted and encouraged to come to Christ, to believe in Christ, to rest and stay their souls on Christ for mercy here and glory hereafter. A very precious word for the worst of sinners to hang on is Ps 68:18. The726 Psalmist, speaking of Christ, says, “You have ascended on high; You have led captives away. You have received gifts for men, even for the rebellious, that the Lord God may dwell among them.”

What if you are a rebellious child or a rebellious servant? What if you are a rebellious swearer, a rebellious drunkard, a rebellious Sabbath-breaker, etc.? Yet Christ has received gifts for you, even for the rebellious. He has received the gift of pardon, the gift of righteousness, indeed all the gifts of the Spirit, for you, so that your heart may be made a delightful house for God to dwell in.

Bodin has a story about a great rebel who had raised a great, strong party against a Roman emperor. The emperor makes a proclamation that whoever could bring in the rebel, dead or alive, would have a great sum of money. The rebel, hearing of this, comes and presents himself before the emperor and demands the sum of money. “Now,” says the emperor, “if I put him to death, the world will say I did it to save my money.” And so he pardons the rebel and gives him the money. Ah sinners! Shall a heathen do this, who had only a drop of mercy and compassion in him? And will not Christ do much more,727 who has all fullness of grace, mercy, and glory in himself? Surely his heart yearns toward the worst of rebels. Ah! If you+ will only come in, you+ will find him ready to pardon, indeed one728 made up of pardoning mercy. Oh, the readiness and willingness of Jesus Christ to receive the greatest rebels into favor!

The father of mercies met, embraced, and kissed that prodigal mouth which came from feeding with swine and kissing harlots. Ephraim had729 committed idolatry and had backslidden from God; he was guilty of lukewarmness and unbelief, etc. Yet God says, “Ephraim is My dear son, a delightful730 child. My heart yearns for him; I will have mercy” (or rather, as it is in the original, I will have mercy, mercy) “on him, declares the Lord.” “Well,” says God, “Though Ephraim is guilty of crimson sins, yet he is a son, a dear son, a precious son, a delightful child. Though he is black with filth and red with guilt, yet my heart yearns for him; I will have mercy, mercy on him.” Ah sinners! If this tender heart of mercy does not melt, win, and draw you+, justice will be a swift witness against you+ and will make you+ lie down in eternal misery for kicking against such tender mercy.

Christ continues to hang out, as that warlike Scythian once did, a white flag of grace and mercy to returning sinners who humble themselves at his feet for favor. But if sinners hold out, Christ will put out his red flag, his bloody flag, and then they will die forever by a hand of justice. Sinners, there is no way to avoid perishing by Christ’s iron rod but by kissing his golden scepter.

The fourth remedy against this device of Satan is to consider that Jesus Christ has nowhere in all the Scripture excluded the worst of sinners who are willing to receive him, to believe in him, and to rest on him for happiness and blessedness. Ah sinners! Why should you+ be more cruel and unmerciful to your+ own souls than Christ is? Christ has not excluded you+ from mercy; why should you+ exclude your+ own souls from mercy? Oh, that you+ would dwell often on that choice Scripture, John 6:37:731 “Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out” (or, as the original has it, I will not cast out). “Well,” says Christ, “if any man will come, or is coming, to me, let him be more sinful or less, more unworthy or less; let him be ever so guilty, ever so filthy, ever so rebellious, ever so leprous, etc. Yet if he will only come, I will not, not, not cast him off.” The same is set forth in 1 Cor 6:9, 10, 11:732 “Do you+ not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God. And that is what some of you+ were. But you+ were washed, you+ were sanctified, you+ were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.”

Ah sinners! Do not think that he who has received such notorious sinners to mercy will reject you+. He is733 “the same yesterday and today and forever.”

Christ was born in an inn, to show that he receives all comers. His garments were divided into four parts, to show that from whatever part of the world we come, we will be received. If we are naked, Christ has robes to clothe us; if we are homeless, Christ has room to lodge us. That is a choice Scripture, Acts 10:34, 35:734 “Then Peter began to speak: ‘I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism, but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.’”

The three languages that were written on the cross, Greek, Latin, and Hebrew, to witness that Christ was735 the King of the Jews, each in its own idiom affirms this singular axiom: that Christ is an all-sufficient Savior; and a threefold cord is not easily broken. The apostle puts this beyond doubt in Heb 7:25:736 “Therefore He is able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.” Now he would not be an all-sufficient Savior if he were not as able to save the greatest sinners as the least. Ah sinners, tell Jesus Christ that he has not excluded you+ from mercy, and that therefore you+ are resolved to sit, wait, weep, and knock at the door of mercy until he says, “Souls, take heart! Your+ sins are forgiven, your+ persons are justified, and your+ souls will be saved.”

The fifth remedy against this device of Satan is to consider that the greater a sinner you are, the dearer you will be to Christ when he sees you as the fruit of the anguish of his soul. Isa 53:11:737 “He will see the fruit of the anguish of His soul and be satisfied.” The more dearly we pay for anything, the dearer that thing is to us. Christ has paid most, and prayed most, and sighed most, and wept most, and bled most for the greatest sinners; and therefore they are dearer to Christ than others who are less sinful. Rachel was738 dearer to Jacob than Leah, because she cost him more; he obeyed, endured, and suffered more by day and by night for her than for Leah. Ah sinners! The greatness of your+ sins only sets off the freeness and riches of Christ’s grace, and the freeness of his love. This makes heaven and earth ring with his praise: that he loves those who are most unlovely, that he shows most favor to those who have sinned most highly against him. This might be shown by various instances in Scripture, such as Paul, Mary Magdalene, and others. Who sinned more against Christ than these? And who had sweeter and choicer manifestations of divine love and favor than these?

The sixth remedy against this device of Satan is to consider seriously that the longer you+ keep away from Christ, the greater and stronger your+ sins will grow. All divine power and strength against sin flows from the soul’s union739 and communion with Christ. While you+ keep away from Christ, you+ keep away from that strength and power which alone is able to make you+ trample down strength, lead captivity captive, and slay the Goliaths that defy Christ. It is only faith in Christ that makes a740 man triumph over sin, Satan, hell, and the world. It is only faith in Christ741 that binds the strong man hand and foot, that stops the flow of blood, that makes a man strong in resisting and happy in conquering. Sin always dies most where faith lives most; the most believing soul is the most mortified soul. Ah sinner! Remember this: there is no way on earth to be effectually rid of the guilt, filth, and power of sin but by believing in a Savior. It is not resolving, it is not complaining, it is not mourning, but believing, that will make you divinely victorious over that body of sin which until now has been too strong for you, and which will certainly be your ruin if it is not ruined by a hand of faith.

The seventh remedy against this device of Satan is to consider wisely that, as there is nothing in Christ to discourage the greatest sinners from believing in him, so there is everything in Christ that may encourage the greatest sinners to believe in him, to rest and lean on him for all happiness and blessedness. If you+ look at his nature, his disposition, his names, his titles, his offices as King, priest, and742 prophet, you+ will find nothing to discourage the greatest sinners from receiving743 him, from believing on him. Christ is the greatest good, the choicest good, the chief good, the most suitable good, the most necessary good. He is a pure good, a real good, a total good, an eternal good, and a soul-satisfying good. Sinners, are you+ poor? Christ744 has gold to enrich you+. Are you+ naked? Christ has royal robes; he has white garments to clothe you+. Are you+ blind? Christ has eye salve to enlighten you+. Are you+ hungry? Christ will be manna to feed you+. Are you+ thirsty?745 He will be a well of living water to refresh you+. Are you+ wounded? He has balm under his wings to heal you+. Are746 you+ sick? He is a physician to cure you+. Are you+ prisoners? He has laid down a ransom for you+. Ah sinners! Tell me, tell me, is there anything in Christ to keep you+ from believing? No. Is there not everything in Christ that may encourage you+ to believe in him? Yes. Oh, then believe in him, and then “though your+ sins are like scarlet, they will be as747 white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.” More than that, your+ iniquities will then be forgotten as well as748 forgiven; they will be remembered no more. God will cast them behind his back; he will hurl them into the bottom of the sea.

The eighth and last remedy against this device of Satan is to consider seriously the absolute necessity of believing in Christ. Heaven is too holy and too hot to hold unbelievers; their lodging is prepared in hell. Rev 21:8:749 “But to the cowardly and unbelieving,” etc., “their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. This is the second death.” “Unless you+ believe that I am He,” says Christ,750 “you+ will die in your+ sins.” And he who dies in his sins must go to judgment, and to hell, in his sins. Every unbeliever is a condemned man: “Whoever does not believe,” says John, “has already been condemned, because751 he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.” And “whoever does not752 believe the Son will not see life. Instead, the wrath of God remains on him.” Ah sinners! The law, the gospel, and your+ own consciences have passed the sentence of condemnation on you+, and there is no way to reverse the sentence but by believing in Christ. And therefore my counsel is this: stir753 yourselves+ up to lay hold on the Lord Jesus, and look up to him, and wait on him from whom every good and perfect754 gift comes, and give him no rest until he has given you that jewel, faith, which is worth more than heaven and earth, and which will make you happy in life, joyful in death, and glorious in the day of Christ. And so much for the remedies against this first device of Satan, by which he keeps thousands from believing in Christ.

2. Unworthiness

The second device that Satan has to keep poor sinners from believing, from embracing a Savior, is,

BY suggesting to them their unworthiness. “Ah!” says Satan. “As you are worthy of the greatest misery, so you are unworthy of the least crumb of mercy. What, do you think,” says Satan, “that Christ will ever acknowledge, receive or embrace such an unworthy wretch as you are? No, no. If there were any worthiness in you, then indeed Christ might be willing to be welcomed by you. You are unworthy to welcome Christ into your house; how much more unworthy are you to welcome Christ into your heart!” etc.

Now the remedies against this device of Satan are as follows.

The first remedy against this device of Satan is to consider seriously that God has nowhere in Scripture required any worthiness in man before believing in Christ. If you+ make a diligent search through all of Scripture, you+ will not find, from755 the first line in Genesis to the last line in Revelation, one word that declares756 that God requires any worthiness in man before the soul believes in Christ, before the soul leans and rests on Christ for happiness and blessedness. Why then should that be a bar and hindrance to your faith which God nowhere requires of you before you come to Christ, so that you may have life? Ah sinners! Remember that Satan raises your+ unworthiness as an objection against you+ only out of a design to keep Christ and your+ souls apart forever. And therefore, in the face of all your+ unworthiness, rest on Christ, come to Christ, believe in757 Christ, and you+ will be happy forever.

The second remedy against this device of Satan is to consider wisely that no one ever received Christ, embraced Christ, or obtained mercy and pardon from Christ, but unworthy souls. Tell me, what worthiness was there in Matthew, Zacchaeus, Mary Magdalene, Manasseh, Paul and Lydia before their coming to Christ, before their faith in Christ? Surely none. Ah sinners! You+ should reason like this: “Christ has bestowed the choicest mercies, the greatest favors, the highest dignities, the sweetest privileges on unworthy sinners. And therefore, O our souls, do not faint, do not despair, but patiently and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord. Who can tell but that free grace and mercy may yet shine forth on us, though we are unworthy, and give us a portion among those worthies who are now triumphing in heaven?”

The third remedy against this device of Satan is this: if the soul will keep away from Christ until it is worthy, it will never take hold of Christ, it will never embrace Christ, it will never be one with Christ; it must lie down in everlasting758 sorrow. God has laid up all worthiness in Christ, so that man may know where to find it and may go out after it. There is no way on earth to make unworthy souls worthy but by believing in Christ. Believing in Christ will make759 you, who were slaves, worthy sons; it will760 make you, who were enemies, worthy friends, etc. God will count no one worthy, nor call anyone worthy, nor deal with anyone as worthy, but believers, who are made761 worthy by the worthiness of Christ’s person, righteousness, satisfaction and intercession, etc.

The fourth and last remedy against this device of Satan is to consider solemnly that if you+ make a diligent search into your+ own hearts, you+ will find that it is the pride and folly of your+ own hearts that drives you+ to bring a worthiness to Christ. Oh, you+ would gladly bring something to Christ that might make you+ acceptable to him; you+ are unwilling to come empty-handed. The Lord cries out, “Come,762 all you+ who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you+ without money, come, buy, and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!”

“Why spend your+ money on763 that which is not bread, and your+ labor on that which does not satisfy?”

Here the Lord calls on moneyless souls, on penniless souls, on unworthy souls, to come and partake of his precious favors freely. But sinners are proud and foolish, and because they have no money, no worthiness to bring, they will not come, though he sweetly invites them. Ah sinners! What is more just than that you+ should perish forever, you+ who prefer husks among swine to the milk and wine, the sweet and precious things of the gospel that are freely and sweetly offered to you+, etc.? Well, sinners, remember this: it is not so much the sense of your unworthiness as your pride that keeps you away from a blessed embracing of the Lord Jesus.

3. Lack of Preparation

The third device that Satan has to keep poor sinners from believing in Christ, from embracing Christ, from resting on Christ, etc. is,

BY suggesting to them the lack of such and such preparations and qualifications. Satan says, “You are not prepared to receive Christ; you are not humbled and justified in this way and that; you are not heartsick of sin; you have not been under horrors and terrors as such and such people have been. You must wait until you are prepared and qualified to receive the Lord Jesus,” etc.

Now the remedies against this device of Satan are as follows.

The first remedy against this device of Satan is to consider seriously that those who have not been prepared and qualified in this way and that, as Satan suggests, have received Christ, believed in Christ, and been saved by Christ. Matthew764 was called while sitting at the tax booth, and such power went along with Christ’s call that it made him follow. We do not read of any horrors or terrors, etc., that he was under before he was called by Christ. Tell me, what preparations and qualifications were found in Zacchaeus, Paul, the765 jailer, and Lydia before their conversion? God brings some in by the sweet and still voice of the gospel, and usually those who are brought in to Christ this way are the sweetest, humblest, choicest and most fruitful Christians. God is a free agent, to work by law or gospel, by smiles or frowns, by presenting hell or heaven to sinners’ souls. God thunders from Mount Sinai on some souls, and conquers them by thundering. God speaks to others in a still voice, and by that conquers them. You+ who are brought to Christ by the law, do not judge and condemn those who are brought to Christ by the766 gospel; and you+ who are brought to Christ by the gospel, do not despise those who are brought to Christ by the law. Some are brought to Christ by fire, storms and tempests, others by easier and gentler breezes of the Spirit. The Spirit is free in the works of767 conversion, and like the wind, it blows when, where and how it pleases. Thrice happy are those souls that are brought to Christ, whether it is on a winter’s night or on a summer’s day.

The second remedy against this device of Satan is to dwell solemnly on the following Scriptures, which clearly show that poor sinners who are not prepared and qualified in this way and that to meet with Christ, to receive and embrace the Lord Jesus Christ, may nevertheless believe in Christ, and rest and lean on him for happiness and blessedness, according to the gospel. Read the first chapter of Proverbs from verse 20 to the end, the first eleven verses of Proverbs 8, the first six verses of Proverbs 9, the first fourteen verses of Ezekiel 16, John 3:14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 36, and Revelation 3:15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20. Here the Lord Jesus Christ stands knocking at the Laodiceans’ door. He would gladly have them dine with him, and dine with them himself; that is, that he and they might have intimate communion and fellowship with one another.

Now tell me, what preparations or qualifications did these Laodiceans have to receive Christ? Surely none. For they were lukewarm; they were neither cold nor hot; they were wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked. And yet Christ, to show his free grace and his stooping love, invites the very worst of sinners to open to him, though they were in no way prepared or qualified like this to receive him, etc.

The third remedy against this device of Satan is to consider seriously that the Lord nowhere in all of Scripture requires such and such preparations768 and qualifications before men come to Christ, before they believe in Christ, or receive or embrace the Lord Jesus Christ. Believing, believing in Christ, is the great thing that God presses on sinners throughout Scripture, as all who know anything of Scripture know.

Objection. But does not Christ say, “Come769 to Me, all you+ who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you+ rest”? To this I will give these three answers.

1. Though the invitation is to those who labor and are heavy laden, yet the promise of giving rest is made to coming, to believing.

2. I answer that all this Scripture proves and shows is that those who labor under sin as under a heavy burden,770 and who are laden with the guilt of sin and the sense of God’s displeasure, ought to come to Christ for rest. But it does not prove that only such must come to Christ, nor that all men must be burdened like this, and laden with the sense of their sins and the wrath of God, before they come to Christ. When poor sinners are under the sense of sin and the wrath of God, they are prone to run from one created thing to another, and from duty to duty, and from ordinance to ordinance, to find rest; and if they could find it in anything or any created thing, Christ would never hear from them. But here the Lord sweetly invites them, and to encourage them, he binds himself to give them rest. “Come,” says Christ, “and I will give you+ rest. I will not show you+ rest, nor merely tell you+ of rest, but I will give you+ rest. I am faithfulness itself and cannot lie: I will give you+ rest. I, who have the greatest power to give it, the greatest will to give it, the greatest right to give it: come, laden sinners, and I will give you+ rest.” Rest is the most desirable good, the most suitable good, and to you+ the greatest good. “Come,” says Christ; that is, “Believe in me and I will give you+ rest. I will give you+ peace with God and peace with conscience; I will turn your+ storm into an everlasting calm; I will give you+ such rest as the world can neither give to you+ nor take from you+.”

3. I answer: no one Scripture expresses the whole mind of Christ. Therefore just compare this one Scripture with the various Scriptures laid down in the second remedy mentioned above, and it will clearly appear that though men are not burdened and laden with their sins like this, and filled with horror and terror, yet they may come to Christ; they may receive and embrace the Lord Jesus Christ.

The fourth and last remedy against this device of Satan is to consider that all the trouble for sin, all the sorrow, shame and mourning, etc., that is acceptable to God, delightful to God and prevails with God, flows from faith in Christ, as the stream does from the fountain, as the branch does from the root, as the effect does from the cause. Zech 12:10: “They will look on771 Me, the One they have pierced. They will mourn for Him.” All gospel mourning772 flows from believing: they will first look, and then mourn. All who know anything know this, that “everything that is not from faith is sin.” Until men have faith in Christ, their best services are only glorious sins.

4. Christ’s Unwillingness

The fourth device that Satan has to keep Christ and a sinner apart, to keep a poor sinner from believing in Christ, from embracing Christ, etc. is,

BY suggesting to the sinner Christ’s unwillingness to save. “It is true,” says Satan, “Christ is able to save you, but is he willing? Surely, though he is able, yet he is not willing to save such a wretch as you are, who have trampled his blood under your feet, and who have been in open rebellion against him all your days,” etc.

The remedy against this device of Satan is to consider briefly these few things.

1. The great journey that he has taken from heaven to earth, on purpose to save sinners, strongly demonstrates his willingness to save them. Matt 9:13: “I have not come to call the773 righteous, but sinners to repentance.” 1 Tim 1:15: “This is a trustworthy saying, worthy774 of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.”

2. His laying aside his glory in order to save sinners declares his willingness to save them. He leaves his Father’s bosom, he puts off his glorious robes, he lays aside his glorious crown, and he bids farewell to his shining courtiers, the angels. And all this he does so that he may accomplish the salvation of sinners.

3. That sea of sin, that sea of wrath, that sea of trouble, that sea of blood775 that Jesus Christ waded through, so that sinners might be pardoned, justified, reconciled, and saved, strongly proves his willingness to save sinners.

4. His sending his ambassadors early and late to woo and entreat sinners776 to be reconciled to him shows with open mouth his readiness and willingness to save sinners.

5. His complaints against those who refuse him, who turn their backs on him, and who will not be saved by him strongly declare his willingness to save them. “He came to His own,777 and His own did not receive Him.” So in John 5:40: “Yet you+ refuse to come778 to Me to have life.”

6. The joy and delight that he takes in the conversion of sinners demonstrates his willingness that they should be saved. Luke 15:7: “I tell779 you+ that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.” God the Father rejoices at the return of his prodigal son. Christ rejoices to see the fruit of the anguish of780 his soul. The Spirit rejoices that he has another temple to dwell in, and the angels rejoice that they have another brother to delight in, etc.

5. God’s Secret Decrees

The fifth device that Satan has to keep a sinner and Christ apart, is,

BY working on a sinner to think more on the secret decrees and counsels of God than on his own duty. “Why do you need to busy yourself about receiving, embracing, and welcoming Christ?” says Satan. “If you are elected, you will be saved; if not, all that you can do will do you no good.” Indeed, he will work on the soul not only to doubt its election, but to conclude that he is not elected, and that therefore, let him do what he can, he will never be saved.

Now the remedies against this device of Satan are these.

The first remedy is to consider seriously that neither all the angels in heaven, nor all the men on earth, nor all the devils in hell can say that you are not an elect person, a chosen vessel. You may be confident of this: God never made Satan one of his Privy Council. God never acquainted him with the names or persons of those on whom he has set his love to eternity, etc.

The second remedy against this device of Satan is, to concern yourself with what you have to do. Secret things belong to the Lord, but revealed781 things belong to you. Your work, sinner, is to be resolute in believing and in returning to the Lord. Your work is to cast yourself on Christ, to lie at his feet, to wait on him in his ways, and to give him no rest till he says, “Sinner, I am your portion, I am your salvation, and nothing will separate you and me.”
